scope: Read-only source review of the stable portable two-time recomputer and README. No model outputs/gradients read; no source edits, tests, builds, or reruns.
checked_semantics: Portable objective is Jmid+Jterminal, with FP64 state arrays and the fixed once-rounded FP32 cotangents promoted to FP64.

The reused old lambda128 is provenance-checked as the prefix160 output at gradient_control_step=128. The first new prefix input is checked bytewise against cast32(promote64(old lambda128)+promote64(q128)); lower three inputs must equal the prior new FP32 output.

Full dAD is dot(v, new_g0_f32 promoted). Midpoint incremental dAD is dot(v, FP64(new_g0_f32)-FP64(old_terminal_g0_f32)); vector subtraction occurs after promotion. Partial prefix window dots are not used as global dAD.

Full and midpoint finite differences are computed separately with frozen eta values, shared max(abs(dFD),abs(dAD)) denominators without a floor, per-component plateau checks, one-sided gaps, and separate signal floors. The full two-term signal scale uses the sum of both norm bounds; the midpoint uses its single-term bound.
The analyzer preserves state-only replay, no global exact-FP64 gradient, no second full gradient replay, no general smoothness claim, and reports local cast/injection residuals only as diagnostics.

Raw collection verifies the four new prefixes against the retained baseline bytes, receipts, inputs, source/executable/protocol, pullback role, and exact Fortran FP64-to-FP32 cast; portable mode verifies NPZ/schema hashes and reproduces the stored arrays.
scope_boundary: This is only a stable source/meaning review. The four-prefix chain and two-time numerical results remain subject to the later actual-data review. No midpoint FD numeric results were read.
